items.stem: Define the term 'internal finance'.
items.answer: Finance raised from within the business, such as retained earnings, the sale of assets and reductions in working capital.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Finance raised from within the business, such as retained earnings, the sale of assets and reductions in working capital. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of using retained earnings to finance expansion.
items.answer: Advantage: there is no interest to pay and no loss of control. Disadvantage: the amount is limited to past profits and shareholders receive lower dividends.
items.markingKey: 1 mark advantage, 1 mark explanation; 1 mark disadvantage, 1 mark explanation. [4]

items.stem: Explain how a business could raise finance by reducing its working capital.
items.answer: It can reduce inventory and collect cash from customers faster, releasing cash that was tied up in current assets.
items.markingKey: 1 mark reduce inventory/receivables; 1 mark releases cash. [2]

items.stem: Green Valley Dairy Co-operative is a co-operative based in Pune, India. It collects milk from 900 member farmers and makes yoghurt and cheese and employs about 80 people. The members are arguing about how much of the profit to reinvest. Explain the internal sources of finance available to Green Valley Dairy.
items.answer: Points to develop for Green Valley Dairy: internal finance comes from within the business; retained earnings from past profits; sale of unused assets or sale and leaseback; releasing cash from working capital.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: internal finance comes from within the business. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Green Valley Dairy (agriculture and food processing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. retained earnings from past profits; sale of unused assets or sale and leaseback. [3]

One game earns 70% of its revenue and its popularity is starting to fall. Explain the internal sources of finance available to Han River Games.
items.answer: Points to develop for Han River Games: internal finance comes from within the business; retained earnings from past profits; sale of unused assets or sale and leaseback; releasing cash from working capital.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: internal finance comes from within the business. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Han River Games (video game development). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. retained earnings from past profits; sale of unused assets or sale and leaseback. [3]

items.stem: Hamid Engineering is a private limited company in Lahore, Pakistan with about 150 staff. It makes pumps and valves for farms and factories. Its factory is working at full capacity and some orders are delivered late. Evaluate whether Hamid Engineering should use internal sources of finance to fund the launch of solar-powered water pumps.
items.answer: For: no interest or loss of control; quick to access; no external approval needed. Against: may not be enough; lower dividends; reduces cash buffer. Judgement: for Hamid Engineering it depends mainly on the amount needed, and also on past profitability.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Hamid Engineering: engineering, about 150 employees, private limited company in Pakistan; its factory is working at full capacity and some orders are delivered late). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. no interest or loss of control; quick to access; no external approval needed; arguments against, e.g. may not be enough; lower dividends; reduces cash buffer. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the amount needed; past profitability; shareholders' expectations. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Hamid Engineering. [10]

items.stem: Define the term 'bank overdraft'.
items.answer: An arrangement with a bank allowing a business to spend more than it has in its account, up to an agreed limit.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – An arrangement with a bank allowing a business to spend more than it has in its account, up to an agreed limit. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of a bank overdraft.
items.answer: Advantage: it is flexible – the business borrows only what it needs and pays interest only on that. Disadvantage: interest rates are high and the bank can demand repayment at short notice.
items.markingKey: 1 mark advantage, 1 mark explanation; 1 mark disadvantage, 1 mark explanation. [4]

items.stem: Explain how debt factoring improves a business's cash flow.
items.answer: The factor pays most of the value of the receivables immediately, so the business does not have to wait for customers to pay.
items.markingKey: 1 mark immediate cash; 1 mark no waiting for customers. [2]

items.stem: Nile Pharma plc is a public limited company based in Cairo, Egypt. It manufactures generic medicines for hospitals and pharmacies in Africa and the Middle East and employs about 1,800 people. Most of its raw ingredients are imported and paid for in US dollars. Explain the short-term sources of finance available to Nile Pharma.
items.answer: Points to develop for Nile Pharma: short-term finance is repaid within a year; bank overdraft for flexible borrowing; trade credit from suppliers; debt factoring to receive cash from receivables.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: short-term finance is repaid within a year. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Nile Pharma (pharmaceuticals). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. bank overdraft for flexible borrowing; trade credit from suppliers. [3]

items.answer: Advantage: it does not have to be repaid and no interest is paid. Disadvantage: the original owners lose some control and future profits are shared as dividends.

items.stem: Explain why a new business might find it difficult to obtain a bank loan.
items.answer: It has no trading record and may have few assets to offer as security, so the bank sees it as high risk.
